tier_reason: The repo ships benchmark code that times the same rank/select queries on this code (bitmap_bench.cc, bitmap_bench_word.cc) and on SDSL (bitmap_bench_sdsl.cc) with stated flags, but it publishes no numbers or CPU model. The only numbers are in arXiv preprint 1706.00990, which is blocked here and known only from search snippets (2x-4x on 64-bit words; 2.2x-6x over CS-Poppy and SDSL), so C stays with a snippet-only caveat.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (arXiv 1706.00990, not opened): PTSelect, a 4-instruction machine-word select (PDEP + TZCNT), is 2x-4x faster than the previous state-of-the-art 64-bit word select; select on bit vectors is 2.2x-6x faster than CS-Poppy and SDSL.
corrections.caveats: Speedup numbers come only from search snippets of arXiv preprint 1706.00990 (arXiv and a third-party summary blog are blocked here). The README is one line with no numbers, and no CPU model appears in the repo. The repo is a GitHub fork of efficient/rankselect (CMU's CS-Poppy code, Apache-2.0, copyright 2013 CMU); this fork adds PTSelect (select64_pdep_tzcnt in popcount.h, used by select64) and the SDSL benchmark. It needs a Haswell-or-later CPU with BMI2, although the Makefile passes only -mpopcnt -msse4 because PDEP/TZCNT come in through inline asm. Timing uses gettimeofday. It bundles an older SDSL version (2017). Newer work (pasta bit_vector, sux) is already catalogued and likely faster. Preprint; peer-review status not verified.

notes: Record mostly accurate. Repo is a GitHub fork of efficient/rankselect (set is_fork_of). Last commit 2017-04-14 ('using pdep-tzcnt select.') confirmed; license Apache-2.0 confirmed from the LICENSE file.
